topicName: Multi-Region Design Patterns and Traffic Manager
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Multi-Region Design Patterns and Traffic Manager in Azure"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Building highly available and resilient cloud applications requires distributing workloads across multiple geographic regions. Azure Traffic Manager, combined with robust multi-region design patterns, enables organizations to achieve high availability, disaster recovery, and optimal performance for global users."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Azure Traffic Manager"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure Traffic Manager is a DNS-based traffic load balancer. It enables you to distribute traffic globally to your public-facing application endpoints. Traffic Manager uses the Domain Name System (DNS) to direct client requests to the most appropriate service endpoint based on a routing method and the health status of the endpoints."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Multi-Region Design Patterns"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Active-Passive (Disaster Recovery): Primary region handles all live traffic while a secondary region remains idle or runs minimal resources until failover is triggered."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Active-Active (Performance and Scale): Multiple regions actively process requests simultaneously, reducing latency and sharing the computational load."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Geographic Routing: Users are routed to specific regional endpoints based entirely on their geographic location to comply with data residency laws or optimize localized experiences."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step-by-Step Implementation Guide"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Follow these Azure CLI commands to create a Traffic Manager profile and configure endpoints for a multi-region deployment."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"az network traffic-manager profile create --name MyTrafficManagerProfile --resource-group MyResourceGroup --routing-method Priority --dns-name MyGlobalApp --ttl 30"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Next, add the primary regional endpoint to the Traffic Manager profile with a higher priority (lower numerical value)."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"az network traffic-manager endpoint create --name PrimaryEndpoint --profile-name MyTrafficManagerProfile --resource-group MyResourceGroup --type azureEndpoints --target-resource-id /subscriptions/{sub-id}/resourceGroups/MyResourceGroup/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/primary-webapp --priority 1"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, add the secondary failover endpoint with a lower priority value."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"az network traffic-manager endpoint create --name SecondaryEndpoint --profile-name MyTrafficManagerProfile --resource-group MyResourceGroup --type azureEndpoints --target-resource-id /subscriptions/{sub-id}/resourceGroups/MyResourceGroup/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/secondary-webapp --priority 2"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Monitoring and Health Checks"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Traffic Manager monitors the health of your endpoints. If an endpoint is deemed unhealthy, Traffic Manager automatically redirects traffic to the healthy secondary region. Ensure your web applications expose a dedicated health check endpoint (such as /healthz) that validates database connectivity and dependent services."}]
